questions.question: Which four orchestration patterns does the lesson list?
options: Sequential, parallel, distributed, and federated, chosen per deployment target
Plan, act, reflect, and refine within a fixed four-step iteration loop
Supervisor-worker, swarm/peer-to-peer, hierarchical, and debate
Push, pull, batch, and stream, chosen per transport protocol
questions.explanation: Supervisor-worker, swarm, hierarchical, and debate recur across 2026 frameworks.

questions.question: What is the 2026 LangChain recommendation regarding supervision?
options: Always use create_supervisor, since it is now the only supported routing mechanism
Avoid supervision entirely and let specialists route themselves without any hub
Run supervisors on dedicated GPU instances kept fully separate from the specialist agents
Prefer direct tool calls over create_supervisor for finer context-engineering control
questions.explanation: Tool-call-based supervision gives you precise control over what each specialist sees.

questions.question: What distinguishes a swarm from a supervisor-worker topology?
options: Swarm has no central router; agents hand off directly via a shared tool surface
Swarm requires dedicated GPU hardware that supervisor-worker topologies do not need
Swarm collapses to a single agent, removing the need for any handoff mechanism
Swarm only runs on a cron schedule, while supervisor-worker runs continuously
questions.explanation: Swarm is peer-to-peer; supervisor centralizes routing through one LLM.

questions.question: When is hierarchical orchestration justified?
options: Always, because hierarchical topology scales for free with no added complexity
When a single supervisor's context budget cannot hold descriptions of all specialists
Only when every specialist agent happens to run on dedicated GPU hardware
Never; the lesson calls nested supervisors an antipattern in every case
questions.explanation: Nested supervisors are for large specialist populations that exceed one supervisor's budget.

questions.question: What is the recommended decision order Anthropic supports?
options: Always start with a hierarchical multi-agent system, since nested supervisors always scale cleanly from day one without any later rework needed
Start with debate first, since cross-critique among proposers catches more errors than any single agent ever could on its own
Start with a single agent plus workflow patterns; add topology only when needed; supervisor before swarm before hierarchical; debate when accuracy beats cost
Start with swarm and contract toward a single agent only once latency completely stops being a concern for the whole team
questions.explanation: Anthropic's guidance is to build the right system for your needs, not the most sophisticated.

questions.question: What is fake hierarchy in this lesson?
options: Mislabelled YAML keys in the orchestrator config that route requests to the wrong specialist
An orchestrator written in TypeScript instead of Python, which the lesson says adds no risk
A test fixture that mocks three supervisor layers purely for automated unit-test coverage and nothing else
Three layers of supervisors because 'enterprise' when there are only two actual teams; collapse it
questions.explanation: Layers that do not correspond to real teams add operational complexity without payoff.
